_comment: Identifiers only - no credentials or secret values. See docs/ecs/state-adoption-plan.md for full context, ordering, and preconditions. Nothing in this file has been imported; it is a reference manifest for Phase A execution, not a record of work done. Every resource address parsed from infrastructure/ecs/environments/staging and its child modules appears exactly once below. CORRECTION (see state-adoption-plan.md section 9.9): a real canary import attempt (module.security_groups.aws_security_group.alb) confirmed that terraform import evaluates enough of the whole configuration graph that ec2:DescribeVpcAttribute on vpc-0fd81b688155ded2b is required for every import, not merely the four SG-rule addresses already marked BLOCKED for ec2:DescribeSecurityGroupRules - none of the classifications below change as a result (all six executable Phase A2 addresses genuinely are import_unchanged), but none of them can actually be imported until this additional permission is granted. The backend prefix remains completely empty and no import has yet succeeded.

counting_methodology.explanation: Terraform's resource count is variable-dependent (count/for_each conditionals). This manifest counts the resource graph that results when every REQUIRED (no-default) variable is set to the value needed to describe this specific live environment, and every OPTIONAL (has-a-default) variable is left at its current repository default. This is the only way to produce a single deterministic total; a different tfvars file could produce a different count.
required_vars_assumed_set_to_live_values: vpc_id, public_subnet_ids, private_subnet_ids (live default VPC and its subnets)
rds_security_group_id (sg-0d4c5eedb2ee21743, enables the 2 count-gated postgres SG rules)
redis_auth_token (required, no default, sourced from Secrets Manager - enables the replication group)
ses_events_queue_arn, ses_events_queue_url, ses_events_dlq_arn (enables ses_consumer's SQS IAM policy and the 3 SQS-based alarm resources)
ses_sending_identity_arn, ses_authorized_from_address (enables the web task role's SES-send policy)
alarm_sns_topic_arn (has no default; required for the cloudwatch_alarms module to be usable at all)
optional_vars_left_at_repository_default: enable_custom_metric_alarms = false (repository default; app-level custom-metric emission does not exist yet) - excludes 4 alarm resource addresses (queue_depth_high, oldest_queued_job_age_high, failed_jobs_high, scheduler_heartbeat_missing) from the total entirely, since their count expression evaluates to 0

resources.prerequisite: Code fix required, and material: live engine is "valkey" (confirmed via aws elasticache describe-replication-groups .Engine), Terraform hardcodes engine="redis". Engine cannot be changed in place - this is a REPLACEMENT-triggering mismatch, previously missed entirely in the prior audit. Also: live engine_version's exact reported value is "7.2.6" (aws elasticache describe-cache-clusters .EngineVersion) vs Terraform default "7.1" (a Redis version string, meaningless for Valkey) - now fixed via the staging-environment var.elasticache_engine_version variable (default "7.1", must be set to "7.2" for this environment - major.minor only; AWS's aws_elasticache_replication_group rejects a major.minor.patch value like "7.2.6" outright for Redis v6+/Valkey - see terraform.tfvars.example), which previously did not exist at all at this level; live parameter group family is "default.valkey7" vs Terraform's hardcoded "default.redis7". All three must be corrected together before import. Additionally add lifecycle { ignore_changes = [auth_token] } (write-only attribute, AWS never returns it) - already present in the module.

Code fix + design decision required: Terraform computes name="${name_prefix}-task-execution"="firmsbase-staging-task-execution"; live role is "firmsbase-staging-ecs-execution-role" (confirmed via aws iam get-role). Beyond the name, live grants execution permissions via the AWS-managed policy AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy plus one narrow inline policy (secrets only); Terraform's task_execution module builds one broader custom inline policy (ECR pull + logs + secrets + KMS) with no managed-policy attachment. These are two different permission-delivery shapes for the same role, not just a naming difference - requires an explicit reviewed decision on which shape to standardize on before import.
resources.notes: Unlike the 7 per-service task roles (structurally new, no live analog), this execution role IS a 1:1 shared-role match with a live resource - corrected from the prior audit's blanket 'no per-role mapping, all unmanaged' treatment, which incorrectly lumped the execution role in with the task role.

resources.prerequisite: Hard stop before any apply (not just import): live service runs assignPublicIp=ENABLED with no NAT gateway anywhere in this VPC (confirmed - default VPC, all-public subnets, sole route table has only an IGW route). Terraform's ecs_service module hardcodes assign_public_ip=false. Applying that in place would cut off all internet egress (ECR/Secrets Manager/CloudWatch Logs/SES/SQS) for every task in the service. Must not apply until the module is fixed to assign_public_ip=true (matching live) or the environment gains real private subnets + NAT. Also: live uses launchType=FARGATE with no capacityProviderStrategy; Terraform uses capacity_provider_strategy exclusively - confirmed non-destructive in-place field swap, safe to accept. Task definition stays pinned per the do_not_import decision above (lifecycle.ignore_changes=[task_definition] already present in the module).
